version_or_date_note: Anvar 2014 and Arjun 2020 interpret s.65B of the Evidence Act 1872. No held judgment interprets the BSA 2023 equivalent.
finding: The proposition is incomplete on a binding judicial point. For electronic records offered as secondary evidence under the Evidence Act 1872, the s.65B(4) certificate is a condition precedent to admissibility (Arjun para 59, approving Anvar). Navjot Sandhu's holding that printouts may be proved under ss.63/65 regardless of s.65B was overruled to that extent; the rest of Navjot Sandhu was not (partial treatment, WSB-T-001; OI-11 on paragraph numbering). The record treats certification as an open 'legal foundation' question, which risks admitting uncertified secondary electronic evidence.
proposed_correction: Add: 'For proceedings governed by the Indian Evidence Act 1872 (applied to courts-martial through AA s.133), electronic records adduced as secondary evidence require a s.65B(4) certificate (Anvar P.V. 2014; Arjun Panditrao Khotkar 2020 para 59). Navjot Sandhu (2005) is not good law on this point. For proceedings on or after 1 July 2024, check the corresponding Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 provision (statutory; Reviewer A).'

finding: The temporal application of ER 2023 rests on no judicial authority, and held material contains none. Isaac addresses only ER 1982 and ER 2008.
